newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire hopes MAM will rethink bid rebuff.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire hopes MAM will rethink bid rebuff.

text.p: Ward Thomas, the chairman of Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc, said on Wednesday he hoped institutional investor Mercury Asset Management would drop its opposition to a 711 million pound take-over by Granada Group Plc.

MAM had been the most vocal of opponents of the 11.75 pounds per share bid, which Thomas said in an interview he had agreed to just over two weeks ago by telephone from a holiday in the south of France.
"I would hope on reflection they will come into line," he said.
MAM, which has a stake of just over 5.0 percent in Yorkshire, might be holding out for a counter bid.
But Thomas said he thought it "highly unlikely" that a third party would emerge with a higher offer.
"There been speculation in newspapers that some foreign entity will come into the arena. I think that's really just poppycock," Thomas said.

He said he had received no indication from United News & Media Plc about how the company would vote its 14 percent stake amid some speculation that managing director Clive Hollick may launch a counter bid.
"I've no idea whether Clive Hollick will or not. But I would have thought his target is much more likely to be HTV Group Plc ," Thomas said.
"But I think if he does, well the shareholders will be happy and MAM will be right and I will be wrong."
Thomas was asked to return to Yorkshire-Tyne Tees three years ago, having retired, after the company's share price collapsed to around 1.20 pounds and it plunged into the red.

Having weathered a restructuring, during which staffing levels fell from around 2,400 to some 1,000, the company made a pre-tax profit of 30.22 million pounds last year. The shares were trading at 11.57p on Wednesday.
"I don't think anybody should be too unhappy about that," Thomas said. "Unless somebody comes into the arena, the price we are getting from Granada is a good price," he noted.
